# t2.1 — Legacy Route and SPA-Serving Parity Contract

## Summary

Keep all URL paths exposed by the 11 legacy PHP route files and their relevant methods functional in the MERN runtime without serving PHP. React aliases resolve the legacy page paths to their corresponding existing screens; Express owns legacy form-action and download compatibility, serves the Vite production bundle, and falls back to the SPA only for browser-page requests. Existing integer request IDs in old queue, status-update, and download links require the DBA-owned legacy-ID mapping.

## Legacy Route Mapping

| Legacy URL / method | Source behavior | MERN route contract |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /`, `GET /index.php` | `index.php:1` redirects to login. | Serve the SPA and preserve both root entry paths. React routes `/` and `/index.php` redirect to `/login.php`, retaining the observed legacy destination; keep the existing clean `/login` route too. |
| `GET /login.php` | `login.php:4-43` renders login. | React alias to the existing `Login` screen; preserve this URL as a valid entry point. |
| `POST /login.php` | Authenticates and redirects administrators to `admin/dashboard.php`, other roles to `dashboard.php`; PHP displays distinct not-found and bad-password feedback. | Compatibility adapter accepts the legacy URL-encoded form and delegates to the same authentication use case, retains the role-specific destination and visible error feedback, and sets only the MERN auth cookie. The React form may continue posting JSON to `/api/auth/login`. |
| `GET /register.php` | `register.php:4-68` renders registration. | React alias to the existing `Register` screen. |
| `POST /register.php` | Creates student/faculty account; duplicate/success/failure feedback; registration does not establish a session. | Compatibility adapter accepts the legacy URL-encoded form, delegates to the registration use case, and must not authenticate the new account as a side effect. Keep the React form on `/api/auth/register`; correct the current MERN auto-login behavior to preserve this contract. |
| `GET /logout.php` | `logout.php:3-8` destroys the session and redirects to login. | React alias to a logout action that calls `POST /api/auth/logout`, then navigates to login. It must clear the MERN cookie, not merely render the login page. |
| `GET /dashboard.php` | Session-gated student dashboard. | React alias to `Dashboard`; retain its authenticated student/faculty outcome. The page reads `/api/dashboard/student`. |
| `GET /submit_request.php` | Session-gated request form. | React alias to `SubmitRequest`. |
| `POST /submit_request.php` | Multipart upload and print-request creation using fields `document`, `copies`, `pages`, `paper_size`, `color_mode`, `print_type`, and `orientation`. | Compatibility adapter routes the legacy multipart request through the same authenticated printing use case as `POST /api/printing`. Preserve field meanings and accept the observed legacy option spellings. Per t2.2, retain raw legacy values and defer storage/display canonicalization to an explicit product decision; do not silently rewrite labels. |
| `GET /queue.php?request_id=…` | Session-gated selected active request, falling back to the latest active request; queue counts and estimate are user-scoped. | React alias to `QueueMonitor`, preserving `request_id`. Continue to accept current Mongo ObjectIds and resolve old integer IDs through the DBA-owned mapping before selecting a request. |
| `GET /history.php?search=…` | Session-gated user-scoped filename substring search and totals. | React alias to `TransactionHistory`; preserve `search` exactly. |
| `GET /admin/dashboard.php` | Admin-gated dashboard. | React alias to `AdminDashboard`; preserve the admin-only outcome and load data from `/api/admin/dashboard`. |
| `GET /admin/requests.php?search=…` | Admin-gated request search. | React alias to `AdminRequests`; preserve `search` and the admin-only outcome. |
| `POST /admin/requests.php` | URL-encoded CSRF-protected form update using `request_id` and `status`, then redirects to `requests.php`. | Compatibility adapter resolves the old request ID and delegates to the same status-update use case as `PATCH /api/admin/requests/:id/status`; retain admin authorization and same-origin/CSRF protection. Existing React controls can continue using the API. |
| `GET /admin/download.php?id=…` | Admin-gated download by legacy integer request ID, with path containment checks. | Keep an Express compatibility handler (not an SPA page): resolve the legacy ID, then reuse the existing authorized and path-safe download behavior. The React admin page continues using `/api/admin/requests/:id/download`. |

This table has 11 PHP route files (root, seven root-level pages/actions, and three admin routes). The non-route PHP database configuration is outside this route table but remains subject to the full-project PHP-removal requirement.

## SPA and HTTP Serving Contract

1. In development, retain Vite's existing client server. Add explicit React Router aliases for the legacy page URLs (including direct `/index.php`) so a direct refresh or bookmark works in both Vite and production. Keep the current clean React URLs for new internal navigation. The legacy download URL is handled by Express before the SPA.
2. In production, build `client/` to `client/dist` and serve that directory with Express static middleware. Do not expose `server/private-uploads` or other private files as static assets.
3. Middleware order: current API/health routes; exact legacy action and download handlers; an `/api` JSON 404; static client assets; then a `GET`/`HEAD` HTML navigation fallback to `client/dist/index.html`; finally a normal 404/error handler. The SPA fallback must never turn unknown `/api` requests or non-navigation methods into HTML.
4. The installed manifest declares Express `^5.3.0`. Express 5 requires a named wildcard; `/{*splat}` includes `/` (unlike `/*splat`). Use the Express-5-compatible pattern if a catch-all route is needed. The fallback must also reject non-HTML requests and `/api` paths.
5. Browser-page authentication behavior belongs in the SPA/API boundary: unauthenticated page visits resolve to the login journey; role-protected actions remain enforced by the API. Do not retain or translate PHP sessions.

## ID and Behavior Dependencies

- Old `request_id` and download `id` values are MySQL integer IDs; the current MERN APIs use Mongo ObjectIds. Per t2.2, preserve them as unique sparse `PrintRequest.legacy_id` values (and preserve source user identity as `User.legacy_id`); compatibility handlers resolve the integer through `PrintRequest.legacy_id` before using the existing ObjectId-based services. Without imported mappings, an old queue link can only fall back to the latest active request and an old download/update cannot identify its target. Do not infer or fabricate IDs.
- Old request forms persist `Black & White`, `Single Sided`, and `Double Sided`; the current React/API uses `Black and White`, `Single-sided`, and `Double-sided`. Per t2.2, keep legacy raw values intact and accept both spellings during import/compatibility handling until a product decision establishes canonical storage/display labels. Pricing and behavior use the corresponding semantic category without rewriting historical text.
- PHP login sessions do not survive the cutover. Users must sign in again using the MERN cookie; this is a runtime boundary change, not a PHP compatibility mode.
- The legacy route aliases do not by themselves resolve other known behavior differences: registration currently authenticates in MERN but not PHP; queue/admin refresh intervals differ; and admin search semantics differ. Preserve the legacy-observed behaviors where required by the approved feature/design contract and include them in later acceptance tests.

## Implementation and Verification Evidence Required

- For all 11 legacy browser-page entry paths (`/`, `/index.php`, and the page paths above), production `GET` and browser refresh return the SPA and render the corresponding page; the protected screens preserve authentication/role outcomes. `/admin/download.php` returns the authorized file response rather than `index.html`.
- Exercise legacy and clean paths with query parameters: history `search`, admin search, and queue `request_id`. Test old integer IDs after `legacy_id` mappings are populated, as well as native Mongo IDs.
- Exercise both legacy form-action paths and API paths for login, registration, multipart submission, and admin status updates. Verify auth cookie/session outcomes, error/success feedback, legacy option-value preservation, and status redirects/updates.
- Verify unknown `/api` routes produce JSON 404s; non-GET navigation requests do not receive the SPA; static assets load; unknown client routes retain the current React wildcard behavior.
- Run the complete root production build and runtime HTTP probes after implementation. This discovery/design task did not modify runtime code, so no build or endpoint test is claimed here.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **HIGH — old integer link resolution depends on migration data.** Mitigation: require DBA-owned unique legacy-ID mapping and test queue, update, and download paths after import.
- **HIGH — blanket SPA fallback can mask API errors or serve HTML for file downloads.** Mitigation: order explicit handlers and API JSON 404 before static/fallback; restrict fallback to HTML navigation methods.
- **WARNING — direct PHP form clients can observe response/feedback drift if only page aliases are added.** Mitigation: preserve legacy POST paths via adapters to shared MERN use cases, rather than duplicating business logic.
- **WARNING — current MERN registration outcome differs from the PHP source.** Mitigation: the registration compatibility behavior is explicit above; implementation must remove auto-login unless product approval changes parity.
